quarterly_data.quarter: Shengyi Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2025 review (annual report): AI ran through the whole year as the main growth driver. In Q1, product certifications built up on the AI side in recent years turned into substantial orders, and with copper and glass-cloth / copper-foil prices rising, management planned a price adjustment at the end of March to pass on raw-material costs; in Q2 server orders kept rising and notebook / game-console HDI orders grew rapidly; in Q4 the AI spill-over took effect - as leading PCB customers hit capacity limits, orders shifted to second-tier customers and the company's orders were full across the board. Facing insufficient capacity, rising copper prices and a glass-cloth supply shortage, senior management visited suppliers to secure resources, accelerated the capacity ramp of Jiangxi phase 2 and carried out several rounds of price adjustments; the company says it exceeded its full-year operating targets.

quarterly_data.quarter: Shengyi Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Raw-material outlook (annual report, company view): since Q4 2025, AI demand has drawn copper-foil and glass-cloth suppliers to switch to high-end copper foil and low-Dk cloth; with LME copper rising fast and copper-foil makers moving to RTF and HVLP products, ordinary HTE copper foil has also become short and its price has climbed rapidly; thin glass-cloth capacity is squeezed by AI demand for low-Dk cloth, with prices jumping 10%-20% a month; and instability in the Middle East, including the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, has made chemical-material supply uncertain. The company says supply-side factors in 2026 will be more complex than ever, bringing large uncontrollable influences on its operating environment.
quarterly_data.figure: thin glass-cloth prices up 10%-20% a month (company statement)

quarterly_data.quarter: Shengyi Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Package substrate materials (annual report): the company completed development of a low-CTE, high-modulus FC-BGA package substrate material system for next-generation HPC and AI chips, aimed at warpage and reliability risks of large packages (>55x55mm) from CTE mismatch and at the dimensional stability and strength needed for high-density routing; it says the product's key performance indicators have reached an internationally leading level and it is striving to land more orders. A packaging film production line was also completed and put into production as planned in 2025. Among its risks, the company says that in the longer run organic-resin materials in high-end high-speed and packaging materials may be disrupted by new ceramic-based and glass-based materials.
